My family has farmed this land in Quzhou for three generations. I have about 8 mu. I know what grows here. The soil is flat, the winters are cold and dry, the summers are hot. There is no question in my mind — I grow wheat in winter and corn in summer, same as always, same as my neighbors.

For wheat, I plant in October after the autumn rains. I use Jimai 22 — the seed station sells it and it does well here. I put down base fertilizer before seeding, then topdress at jointing. I water three times: once before winter sets in to help the roots, once at jointing, once at heading. I spray once for weeds early on and once for rust or aphids if I see them. Rotary tillage before planting, nothing fancy.

For corn, I plant right after the wheat harvest in June. No time to waste — rainy season is short. I use hybrid seed, Zhengdan 958, because it gives better yield. I put fertilizer down at planting and topdress when it's knee-high. I watch the sky — if it rains enough I only water once or twice. I spray for corn borer and for weeds.

I do not grow vegetables for sale. I am too old to do that kind of intensive work and I have no one to help me haul it to market. Wheat and corn I can manage alone with the small tractor I share with my brother-in-law.
